exposure: gut microbiome composition (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacteroides fragilis, butyrate and propionate producers)
stool metabolome (D-glucose, butyrate, propionate, folate biosynthesis pathway, trehalose metabolic pathway)
gene expression of associated virulence factors (invasin, adhesin, flagellin, lipopolysaccharides)
cohort: The study included 63 infants between ages 3 weeks and 12 months with well-defined eczema cases and controls from the Growing Up in Singapore Toward healthy Outcomes (GUSTO) mother-offspring cohort.
finding: Allergen-sensitized atopic eczema infants exhibited an aberrant developmental trajectory of the gut microbiome and stool metabolome, characterized by an early enrichment of *Escherichia coli* and *Klebsiella pneumoniae* (associated with increased stool D-glucose and virulence factors) and a delayed colonization by beneficial *Bacteroides fragilis* and subsequent accumulation of butyrate and propionate producers.
